Marissa —

Quick summary from infra triage (initial):
- Timeline: a runtime rollout that adjusted kernel selection preferences and a quantization fallback rule were deployed to the hosted fleet in a staged push on 2026-02-17 22:10 UTC. The rollout targeted cost-conscious policies for lower-tier model variants and introduced a new kernel ordering optimization intended to prefer int8 kernels on T4-like hardware when sequence lengths exceed ~1k.
- Correlation: Our telemetry shows a rise in token-pps variance for sequences >800 tokens starting 2026-02-18 07:00 PST that lines up with the rollout reaching the cluster serving FastRetails region. There are increased kernel-switch events mid-request (kernel reshuffle) which cause micro-scheduling stalls and KV cache misses.
- Immediate mitigation: We can roll back the kernel-selection override for the affected cluster (takes ~8–12 minutes to ramp) and pin FastRetail to the previous kernel order and quantization profile.

Action plan proposed:
1) Rollback kernel ordering for FastRetails shard and pin model variant to pre-2026-02-17 profile (Vivek). ETA 15–30m to start seeing improvement.
2) Run a targeted canary with identical long-sequence traffic and validate token/sec and error rates (Evelyn + infra).
3) Postmortem: include safe rollout gating (sequence-length aware canaries), and add a fallback that prevents mid-request kernel switches for long outputs.

Ill start the rollback if you authorize.

Vivek Kulkarni
Sr. Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-02-20T16:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production impact — spikes in P99/P95 on hosted API

Marissa / Vivek —

Status update for executive recipients and for FastRetail:
- What happened: A queued runtime optimization changed kernel preference ordering and a quantization fallback rule in a staged release. For very long outputs the runtime may attempt an int8 kernel mid-request which is faster for short sequences but incurs KV cache invalidation + kernel context switches for long sequences; this produced token/s throughput drops and tail-latency regressions (p95/p99).
- What we did: Vivek rolled back the kernel-ordering override for the affected shards at 2026-02-18T11:20 PST; we pinned FastRetails traffic to the pre-change profile. Post-rollback telemetry shows P99 improved from ~2.3s spikes to ~0.9s and token/sec recovered to within 8% of baseline.
- Short-term mitigations (already in progress):
  * Pinning by account for 48 hours for any long-sequence customers while we complete canaries.
  * Turn off mid-request kernel reshuffle feature for hosted clusters serving sequences > 700 tokens.
  * Add alerting to detect sudden rise in kernel-switch events and KV cache miss rate.
- Next steps / ask:
  * Product & Eng to draft a postmortem and updated rollout gating that simulates long-output traffic (owner: Evelyn).
  * Customer-facing note & credits: Marissa to propose a goodwill credit for the incidence window (suggestion: one week of usage credits or a service credit tied to SLA).
  * Exec visibility: Please acknowledge if you want this escalated to the C-suite and the legal procurement team.

I recommend communicating the rollback and the immediate improvements to Craig and scheduling a short post-mortem review with their infra team.

Evelyn Hart
Product Lead, Serving Runtime
evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Redwood Inference
